articles.title: Russian ballistic missiles rock Kyiv as air defenses engaged
articles.body:
Russian ballistic missile attack against Kyiv kills 2, injures 6 after day of drone strikes
Editor's note: This is a developing story and is being updated.
Two people were killed, and six others were injured as Russian ballistic missile explosions rocked Kyiv overnight on Sept. 24.
At the same time missiles were battering the capital, President Volodymyr Zelensky was meeting with members of the U.S. Congress, discussing the recently passed Lindsey Graham law while attending the U.N. General Assembly. 
"Right now, the United States has an opportunity to respond strongly," Zelensky wrote on X. "We need ballistic missile interceptors to protect lives. Sanctions against Russia and those helping it make money must be implemented."
Loud explosions were first heard in the city center of Ukraine's capital at around 1:00 a.m. local time, Editor-in-Chief Olga Rudenko said.
Ukraine's Air Force also warned that a ballistic missile was headed toward Kyiv after an air raid alert had been declared in Kyiv at 12:59 a.m.
"I got woken up by the sound of an explosion, slept through the air raid alert. When I checked my phone, I saw alerts for incoming missiles and went to my hallway as a series of explosions blasted out, one of them set off car alarms near my flat," War Editor Chris York said.
Then another ballistic missile was headed toward Ukraine's capital at 1:27 a.m., the Air Force said.
"It was quiet for about 30 minutes until another wave of ballistic missiles came in, I counted eight explosions," York said.
A third wave of ballistic missile explosions rocked the city again at around 1:52 a.m. local time, he added.
Updates from authorities
Kyiv Mayor Vitali Klitschko said that paramedics were headed to sites in the city's Solomyanskyi, Svyatoshynskyi, and Podilskyi districts as Russian missiles continued to target the city.
In the Dniprovskyi district, debris fell into a residential building courtyard, where there could be people trapped under rubble, he said. Debris also fell onto an administrative building in the district.
"In the Podilskyi district, debris fell on a parking lot near a medical facility. Several cars caught fire. Emergency services are en route," Klitschko said.
Debris from missiles also fell near a maternity hospital, shattering windows and damaging a part of the building's facade, he said
Although there were no casualties in the maternity hospital, one person was killed in a nearby parking lot, Klitschko said, adding that a medical diagnostic center was also damaged.
Russia regularly strikes civilian infrastructure and cities across Ukraine in fatal missile and drone attacks.
The prior day, on Sept. 23, a series of deadly Russian drone strikes on Kyiv killed two people and injured at least 43 others during the morning.
Railway infrastructure, residential buildings, and a historic market were damaged in the Russian attack.
On Sept. 22, Russian jet-powered drones struck Kyiv, injuring at least eight people and hitting sites across several districts of the capital, authorities said.

articles.title: Iran’s president Pezeshkian to address UN general assembly before Zelenskyy takes the stage - live
articles.body:
Venezuela being ‘reborn’, Rodríguez tells UN; Trump greets Xi Jinping ahead of high-stakes US-China summit – live
Acting president says Venezuela returning strongly after ‘setbacks’; Trump meets Chinese leader at US air base ahead of meeting set to include trade, AI and Iran war
Venezuela’s acting president has told the UN her country is coming back strong after “setbacks” this year and thanked Donald Trump for being willing to resume diplomatic relations after the US military spirited her predecessor out of the country.
“Today, Venezuela is being reborn,” Delcy Rodríguez said in addressing the general assembly for the first time since she came to power.
Rodríguez took over in Venezuela after the US military’s raid in January that captured Nicolás Maduro and brought him to the US to face drug trafficking charges.
This is the first trip to the US by a Venezuelan head of state since 2018, when Maduro travelled to New York to take part in the UN general assembly, the Associated Press reports. He is currently being held not far from the organisation’s headquarters as he awaits trial.
“I do not promise you an easy way forward,” Rodríguez said, saying she was addressing her people.
Rebuilding our national soul will be the priority.
Returning to Venezuela for a moment, interim leader Delcy Rodríguez also told the UN her country would hold elections.
“I want to state this very clearly before this general assembly: there will be elections in Venezuela,” she said, while giving no timeline.
Many Venezuelans have been hopeful that the ongoing US-backed political transition talks between the interim government and parts of the opposition would lead to a democratic election, as AFP reports. But those hopes were dented early this month when Donald Trump – speaking shortly after striking a huge oil deal with Caracas – brushed off the notion of a vote in the near future.
Rodríguez echoed those comments at the time.
Rodríguez replaced president Nicolas Maduro after his ouster by US forces in January, and she has served as a pliant ally to Washington since then.
As mentioned earlier, while addressing the UN general assembly she thanked the Trump administration for its “willingness to resume the path of diplomatic relations and cooperation with Venezuela”.
China and US should be partners not rivals, says Xi
Xi Jinping said after arriving that Beijing and Washington should be partners rather than rivals, Chinese state news agency Xinhua is reporting.
With joint efforts, the US visit was sure to be fruitful, Xi said in written remarks, according to Xinhua.
Separately Xi was also quoted as suggesting in his statement that the two sides “should move toward each other and work together to build a stable relationship – one where cooperation is the mainstay, competition is kept within proper limits, differences are managed and peace can be expected”.
On returning to the White House, Donald Trump said of travelling to greet Xi’s plane on arrival: “I think they appreciate it, tremendous people.”
On Xi Jinping’s arrival in the US, his plane was met with a lavish arrival ceremony that included a 30-metre-long red carpet flanked by US service members, a military flyover by two B-1 bombers and a presentation of the flags and national anthems of both countries.
US presidents typically welcome foreign leaders at the White House, but Trump and first lady Melania Trump travelled to the military base just outside Washington DC to personally greet the Chinese leader and his wife Peng Liyuan’s on touching down.
The pageantry will continue with a formal state welcome on the South Lawn of the White House, a private tea with the US president and first lady and a tour of the National Archives, among other events.
Venezuela’s acting president has told the UN her country is coming back strong after “setbacks” this year and thanked Donald Trump for being willing to resume diplomatic relations after the US military spirited her predecessor out of the country.
“Today, Venezuela is being reborn,” Delcy Rodríguez said in addressing the general assembly for the first time since she came to power.
Rodríguez took over in Venezuela after the US military’s raid in January that captured Nicolás Maduro and brought him to the US to face drug trafficking charges.
This is the first trip to the US by a Venezuelan head of state since 2018, when Maduro travelled to New York to take part in the UN general assembly, the Associated Press reports. He is currently being held not far from the organisation’s headquarters as he awaits trial.
“I do not promise you an easy way forward,” Rodríguez said, saying she was addressing her people.
Rebuilding our national soul will be the priority.
More on Scott Bessent saying the US and China had agreed to a two-month extension of their trade war truce, which had been due to expire on 10 November.
The deal came after marathon talks between the US treasury secretary and his Chinese counterpart, vice-premier He Lifeng, in New York on Sunday and in Washington on Wednesday.
The announcement came just as Chinese leader Xi Jinping arrived in the US on Thursday evening for a high-stakes summit with Donald Trump.
“We have agreed today that we will extend what we call the Busan agreement, the economic detente between the two countries that was scheduled to end on November 10th,” Bessent told Fox News.
That is going to be extended until January 10th to give us more time to see what we can do on the economic front.
The truce, which took effect last year, came after Trump struck a deal with Xi. The agreement saw both sides agree to reduce tit-for-tat tariffs and for the US to extend certain tariff exclusions.
Washington had also agreed at the time to suspend responsive actions after an investigation into China’s shipbuilding sector, as AFP reports.
Bessent on Wednesday also flagged the possibility that both sides could reduce tariffs on $30bn of non-sensitive goods.
A selection of pictures here from the cordial greeting given to Xi Jinping and his wife Peng Liyuan from Donald and Melania Trump at Joint Base Andrews, Maryland, outside Washington DC.
US and China agree to extend trade war truce, says Bessent
The US treasury secretary is saying the US and China have agreed to extend “the Busan agreement”.
Scott Bessent’s comments to Fox News came after he met Chinese vice-premier He Lifeng before Xi Jinping’s state visit to Washington this week.
“We met today to see if we could do a bigger deal as opposed to just a series of smaller things,” Bessent was quoted as saying on Wednesday. “We have agreed today that we will extend what we call the Busan agreement.”
The extension would go until 10 January, he said.
The Busan agreement refers to the trade war truce Trump and Xi agreed to in Busan, South Korea, in October last year.
Trump greets Xi at airport in rare personal welcome to US
Xi Jinping has arrived in Washington and been greeted by Donald Trump at the airport instead of waiting for him to drive to the White House.
The decision to greet the Chinese leader there has been reported as showing how far Trump is going to honour China’s leader as he makes his first state visit to the US capital in more than a decade.
Trump and First Lady Melania Trump greeted Xi and his wife Peng Liyuan after the Chinese president descended from his plane at Joint Base Andrews, a military airfield outside Washington, for the start of a three-day state visit.
Iran’s president, Masoud Pezeshkian, turned the tables on Donald Trump, describing the US as the true bully and terrorist in the Middle East while insisting that Iran had always shown a commitment to the negotiating table.In a defiant speech to the UN general assembly in New York, his first since the US and Israel launched an all-out war on Iran, Pezeshkian repeatedly vowed that Tehran would never bend the knee to the US. But he balanced defiance with a willingness to talk, saying: “It must be understood by President Trump and those who seek to bully us that we are ready for dialogue and diplomacy and negotiations but without the language of force.” Here’s Patrick Wintour’s report.
Volodymyr Zelenskyy warned Moscow that Ukraine would strike back and make the coming winter deeply painful for Russia, if the two sides cannot agree a truce on energy attacks before the cold sets in. “Ukrainians understand that this winter could be very harsh for us. But in response, we will have no choice but to make it painful for Russia too,” Zelenskyy told member nations, as he urged leaders to keep choking Russia’s revenues and impede its war efforts.
Zelenskyy also used his address to single out Putin’s role in driving the war, repeatedly describing him derisively as “patient zero” and “the one from whom this idea of war keeps spreading further”. He said: “That is why ’patient zero’ must be stopped. He must be denied the space to act – and the space to spread this evil further.” Ukraine did not choose this war, he reiterated, stressing that partial victory (in Donetsk) would never be enough for Putin.
PolishpresidentKarol Nawrocki warned that without accountability, international law is not more than “a declaration without any real power”. “Russia is destablising the situation in Europe through open aggression, hybrid operations, acts of subversion and sabotage, and by ignoring successive resolutions of this assembly,” he said, adding: “If aggression is not met with an adequate response, it becomes an invitation to repeat it.”
Javier Milei condemned the UN as he warned that Argentina would take “matters into our own hands” in its dispute with Britain over the sovereignty of the Falkland Islands. In a caustic speech, the Argentinian president criticised the UN for being ineffective when it came to the long-running tensions over the British overseas territory in the south Atlantic known in Argentina as the Malvinas. “An organisation that set out to defend the territorial sovereignty of its members decided to look the other way regarding the situation of the Falkland Islands,” Milei said of the UN, adding that Argentina was willing to act unilaterally over recent oil exploration near the territory.
Milei told the assembly that Argentina would “not remain indifferent to those who exploit resources under illegal foreign occupation”. “Argentina is not going to sit around waiting for the UN and the international community to live up to their own mandate,” he said. “We’re going to take matters into our own hands.” Here’s Daniel Boffey’s report.
Syria’s interim president harshly criticized Israel’s occupation of southern Syria and said the Golan Heights is an inseparable part of his country. In a speech to the UN General Assembly, Ahmad al-Sharaa said that Israel has carried out more than 500 air and artillery strikes on the country since he took power nearly two years ago. Israel has also carried out 1,200 land incursions and detained nearly 300 people, he said.
The United States has invited Russian president Vladimir Putin to attend the G20 summit of world leaders being held in Miami in December, US secretary of state Marco Rubio said. “In order to solve problems, you have to meet with the people that you disagree with or the people that you might have some issues with, so we’ve invited president Putin to the G20.
Kenyan president William Ruto argued for the necessity of reforming the UN security council and for greater African representation.
“On the greatest questions of war and peace, five nations possess a power that the other 188 do not,” Ruto said.
Demanding a permanent seat on the council for Africa, he added: “We cannot manage transformation with institutions that refuse to transform themselves.”
Namibian president NetumboNandi-Ndaitwah joined growing calls for a woman to be elected as the next United Nations secretary-general.
Addressing member nations, Nandi-Ndaitwah noted that no woman has held the position since the organisation was established in 1945, and said the UN’s leadership should reflect the gender equality it promotes across the international system.
“Namibia therefore, believes that it is time that a woman is elected as secretary-general of our Organisation,” she said.
Panama calls for region to have permanent seat on UN security council
Earlier, Panama’s president, José Raúl Mulino, also called for for the Latin America and Caribbean region to have a permanent seat on the UN security council.
I wish to reiterate before this general assembly the need for Latin America and the Caribbean to hold positions with greater decision-making power on the security council, specifically a permanent position, as a permanent member of this organization’s security council.
We are a leading region in food, minerals, biodiversity, and [have] a deep commitment to peace and integration.
He urged the UN to address urgent issues including migration and the climate crisis, adding:
We must acknowledge that citizens do not believe these kinds of gatherings benefit them. Herein lies one of the reasons why trust must be restored.
Our conclusion is unequivocal: the world does not need less United Nations; it needs a United Nations that works better.
'We are not the ones seeking confrontation,' says Polish president in face of Russian aggression
Polish president Karol Nawrocki spoke of the grave importance of accountability if there is to be lasting peace and “if international law is to be anything other than a declaration without any real power”.
The absence of accountability in the international community has “sent a signal [to aggressive states] that violations of international law, aggression, and imperialist policies could go unpunished,” he told member nations.
It is precisely this lack of justice - this sort of original sin of the postwar order - that creates space for the return of old aggressive ambitions and methods of operation.
He went on: “Russia is destablising the situation in Europe through open aggression, hybrid operations, acts of subversion and sabotage, and by ignoring successive resolutions of this assembly.”
Contempt for international law must not become the norm.
As a country that neighbours Russia, he said he wanted to make it clear on behalf of Poland that “we are not the ones seeking confrontation”.
We are strengthening our alliances, developing our military, and modernizing its equipment not to wage war, but to prevent it … Our goal is deterrence and defence.
Nato remains the “guarantor of transatlantic security”, he said.
“Russia is carrying out actions aimed at undermining the foundations of international stability,” Nawrocki went on.
If aggression is not met with an adequate response, it becomes an invitation to repeat it.
Russian presidential envoy Kirill Dmitriev is heading to the United States on Wednesday, where he will meet with Trump administration representatives Steve Witkoff, JaredKushner and others, two sources familiar with preparations for the talks have told Reuters.
The sources said that Dmitriev’s visit to the US, which was agreed upon with Vladimir Putin, will take place in New York on the sidelines of the UN general assembly and will follow up on a meeting between Putin and US representatives at the Kremlin earlier this month.
One source told Reuters that the aim of the visit is to keep the Russia-US dialogue and the peace-making effort going.
President of Panama José Raúl Mulino is now up. He kicks off by applauding multiculturalism and the role of the UN in a world of “such volatility”, but calls for greater leadership.
“We must restore trust,” he says, warning that illegal people trafficking was taking a heavy toll on the country socially and economically, but also on some sensitive natural environments in Panama.
“We must make headway together on the key issues,” he says. This includes world trade, with Panama’s canal playing a key global role, but he warns it is increasingly at risk from heavy rain and flooding which is worsening due to the climate crisis, despite Panama being a carbon negative country.
President of the Central African Republic, Faustin-Archange Touadéra, is now on the podium, speaking about the country’s ongoing sectarian conflict and political instability.
“A fragile country needs security for development,” he says, calling for international support. “Peace cannot be decreed, it must be built day after day through dialogue, justice and shared development.”
“Holding out your hand to yesterday’s opponent is not a sign of weakness”, he says.
He also warns about the worsening impacts due to the global climate crisis and calls for a greater role for women in public life to help end instability in the country.

articles.title: “Ukraine Ready to Halt Energy Strikes if Russia Does the Same,” Zelenskyy Says After Trump Meeting
articles.body:
- Category
- War in Ukraine
“Ukraine Ready to Halt Energy Strikes if Russia Does the Same,” Zelenskyy Says After Trump Meeting
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy met with US President Donald Trump in New York on the sidelines of the 81st session of the UN General Assembly on September 22. The leaders held a brief 7-minute meeting with the press before continuing their discussions behind closed doors, which lasted 40 minutes.
Speaking at his personal press conference following the closed-door meeting, Zelenskyy commented on the outcome of the talks and outlined new defense and diplomatic initiatives aimed at securing long-term stability.
We bring you stories from the ground. Your support keeps our team in the field.
His proposals included seeking US authorization for domestic air defense manufacturing, advocating for a mutual energy truce, leveraging American sanctions, and exploring direct trilateral peace talks involving Washington and Moscow.
Addressing air defense needs, Zelenskyy confirmed that military advisor Pavlo Palisa held preliminary discussions with American defense manufacturer Raytheon regarding the domestic production of Patriot air defense systems.
"As a security shield for Ukraine, in any way, we need licenses to begin the prepare production of Patriots," Zelenskyy said, noting that President Donald Trump is "positive with licenses."
While Raytheon expressed readiness to partner, the project relies on official US licensing, which could take a year to eighteen months to operationalize.
To address immediate interceptor shortages, Zelenskyy signed a contract with Germany for 600 Patriot missiles split into two packages. He appealed to the US for urgent missile transfers to protect civilians, stating, "I said very openly because it's deficit, I'm asking United States to help me now, to help our people now, to save our people now," offering to replenish American stockpiles by 2027.
On the diplomatic front, Zelenskyy voiced support for a mutual energy truce as an initial step toward de-escalation, confirming that the US side will convey Kyiv's proposal to Moscow.
"We spoke about how to end the war: we are ready for this. I am not sure that Russia is ready for this. We spoke about an energy truce. We are ready for it. Of course, we are ready to stop strikes on their oil refineries and energy system if they do not strike ours," Zelenskyy stated following his meeting with President Trump.
Clarifying the scope of the proposed energy truce, Zelenskyy emphasized that Washington did not ask Kyiv for any unilateral pause on strikes against Russian energy infrastructure. "We are speaking about an energy truce. If it concerns energy—it means all energy," Zelenskyy explained, noting that a complete arrangement must also cover water supply infrastructure and other critical municipal utilities.
However, the Ukrainian President expressed deep skepticism regarding Moscow's willingness to abide by any standstill, warning the US administration that Russian forces would likely violate the agreement.
"There will be attacks, and Putin will tell you that it happened because of Ukraine," Zelenskyy warned, citing recent Russian strikes as evidence of Moscow using fabricated pretexts to maintain its campaign of aerial bombardment.
Zelenskyy also reiterated his readiness for a direct trilateral summit with US President Donald Trump and Russian leader Vladimir Putin to end the war. "I'm ready anytime when all the sides will be ready," he stated.
Zelenskyy recently proposed a conditional energy de-escalation framework to Western partners, indicating that Kyiv is prepared to halt strikes on Russian refineries if international partners can secure and guarantee a complete end to Russian attacks on Ukraine’s energy, port, and logistics infrastructure.
In a statement, he emphasized that any mutual halt must be reliable, long-term, and enforceable rather than a brief operational pause. Expressing skepticism regarding Moscow’s willingness to abide by an agreement, Zelenskyy warned that Russia might seek temporary relief for its domestic fuel markets ahead of elections before resuming strikes.

articles.title: Poland says Russian military helicopter violated its airspace
articles.body:
Poland says Russian military helicopter violated its airspace
A Russian military Mi-8 helicopter entered Polish airspace on September 23 at 11:08 a.m., the operational command of the Polish army said.
The helicopter, flying from the Kaliningrad region, crossed about 300 meters (984 feet) into Polish airspace and remained there for 42 seconds, the Polish military said.
Poland scrambled fighter jets and put ground forces and equipment on alert. “The nature of the incident indicates that Russia is once again testing the readiness of our air defense,” the command said.
Russia has not yet commented on the incident.
Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk said on September 17 that Russia is planning “hybrid” strikes using missiles and drones against countries that support Ukraine. He claimed that “there is a real risk that drones or other types of missiles may fly into the territory of one or more NATO countries on the eastern flank, even cause destruction.”
Over the past several months, drones have repeatedly entered the airspace of Estonia, Lithuania, and Latvia. In addition, overnight on September 13, Russian forces attacked a gas station near the Yahodyn border crossing on the Polish-Ukrainian border and a passenger train on the Kyiv-Warsaw railway line with drones.

articles.title: Ukraine loses nearly 1,400 troops in special op zone over past 24 hours — Defense Ministry
articles.body:
MOSCOW, September 23. /TASS/. Ukraine has lost approximately 1,380 troops in the special military operation zone over the past 24 hours, the Russian Defense Ministry reported.
According to its statement, Russia’s Battlegroup North eliminated up to 210 Ukrainian personnel, the Battlegroup West eliminated up to 220 enemy troops, the Battlegroup South eliminated up to 225 troops, the Battlegroup Center eliminated more than 410, the Battlegroup East destroyed over 275 troops, and the Battlegroup Dnepr eliminated up to 40 enemy personnel.
Russia carries out coordinated strikes on Ukrainian defense, energy sites
Russian troops carried out coordinated overnight strikes on Ukrainian defense and energy industry facilities, as well as logistics centers, the Defense Ministry reported.
"Last night, the Russian Armed Forces carried out coordinated strikes with drones against facilities in Ukraine’s military-industrial and fuel-energy sectors, logistics centers, and naval vessels operating on behalf of the Ukrainian military," the ministry said in a statement.
Russia hits dry cargo ship with military supplies on its way to Odessa port
The Russian Armed Forces struck a dry cargo ship with military supplies en route to the port of Odessa, the Defense Ministry reported.
"A dry cargo ship delivering military cargo to the port of Odessa was struck at sea," the ministry said in a statement.
Russian forces strike Kiev warehouse storing materials for drone production
The Russian Armed Forces hit a warehouse in Kiev storing materials for drone production, the Defense Ministry reported.
"As a result of the strike, the following targets in Kiev and the Kiev region were hit: a warehouse storing materials for drone production and an industrial enterprise (Tukans LLC) in Vishnevoye (near Kiev), which manufactured drone components," the ministry said in a statement.
Russian forces strike three logistics centers in Odessa
Russian forces hit three logistics centers in Odessa that were storing military cargo, as well as a warehouse in the Odessa Region, the Defense Ministry reported.
"The following targets were struck <…> in the Odessa Region: three logistics centers in the city of Odessa, which were used to store and distribute military and dual-use cargo to supply the Ukrainian military, and a warehouse for drone components in Mirnoye in the Odessa Region," the ministry said in a statement.
Russian air defenses shoot down 514 Ukrainian drones overnight
Air defense forces intercepted and destroyed 514 Ukrainian unmanned aerial vehicles over Russian regions during the past night, the Defense Ministry reported.
"Over the past night, air defense forces on duty intercepted and destroyed 514 fixed-wing unmanned aerial vehicles over the Belgorod, Kursk, Bryansk, Voronezh, Oryol, Kaluga, Lipetsk, Tambov, Ryazan, Nizhny Novgorod, Smolensk, Saratov, Samara, Ulyanovsk, Rostov, Krasnodar Regions, the republics of Crimea, Bashkortostan, Tatarstan, and over the waters of the Sea of Azov and the Black Sea," the ministry said in a statement.
Russian air defenses down 868 Ukrainian fixed-wing drones over past day
Russian air defense forces shot down three guided aerial bombs and 868 Ukrainian fixed-wing unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) over the past day, the Defense Ministry reported.
"Air defense capabilities shot down three guided aerial bombs and 868 fixed-wing unmanned aerial vehicles," the ministry said in a statement.
Overall, the Russian Armed Forces have destroyed 674 Ukrainian warplanes, 284 helicopters, 244,127 unmanned aerial vehicles, 672 surface-to-air missile systems, 31,010 tanks and other armored combat vehicles, 1,780 multiple rocket launchers, 36,547 field artillery guns and mortars and 72,638 special military motor vehicles since the start of the special military operation, the ministry reported.
Russian Black Sea Fleet destroys 3 Ukrainian uncrewed boats in past day
The Russian Navy Black Sea Fleet’s aircraft have destroyed three Ukrainian uncrewed boats over the past day, the Defense Ministry reported.
"The Black Sea Fleet’s aircraft destroyed three uncrewed boats of the Ukrainian armed forces in the northwestern part of the Black Sea," the ministry said in a statement.
Russian forces destroying Ukrainian units trapped in western, eastern parts of Dobropolye
Over the past 24 hours, the Russian Armed Forces continued to destroy Ukrainian units trapped in the western and eastern parts of Dobropolye in the Donetsk People’s Republic (DPR), the Defense Ministry reported.
"Assault units of the Marine Corps group and the 76th Airborne Assault Division continued to destroy Ukrainian army units trapped in the western and eastern parts of Dobropolye," the ministry said in a statement.
Russian forces hit logistics centers, fuel depots used by Ukrainian army
Russian forces struck logistics centers, fuel depots, energy facilities used by the Ukrainian army and temporary deployment areas of Ukrainian troops and foreign mercenaries over the past day, the Defense Ministry reported.
"Operational/tactical aircraft, attack unmanned aerial vehicles, missile troops and artillery of the Russian groups of forces struck logistics centers, fuel depots, energy facilities used by the Ukrainian army, workshops producing unmanned aerial vehicles and their components and temporary deployment sites of Ukrainian armed formations and foreign mercenaries," the ministry said in a statement.
Russian forces liberate Krasny Yar, Potikhonovo communities in Kharkov Region
Russian Battlegroup North units took control over the Krasny Yar and Potikhonovo settlements in the Kharkov Region in the course of the special military operation over the past day, the Defense Ministry reported.
"Units of the Battlegroup North are tightening the ring of encirclement and expanding the external zone of control. As a result of decisive operations, they took control of the Krasny Yar and Potikhonovo communities in the Kharkov Region," according to the ministry’s statement.
Russian army thwarts Ukrainian troops’ attempt to break out of encirclement near Kharkov
Russia’s Battlegroup North has thwarted an attempt by Ukrainian troops to break out of an encirclement in the Kharkov Region near Chyornoye, the Defense Ministry said.
"Enemy units were engaged in the areas of Varvarovka and Grachevka in the Kharkov Region. An enemy attempt to break out of the encirclement from Chyornoye in the Kharkov Region was thwarted," the news release reads.
Russian Armed Forces expand encirclement ring in northwestern part of Dobropolye
Units of Russia’s Battlegroup Center, during their offensive in Dobropolye in the Donetsk People’s Republic, have expanded the external encirclement ring in the northwestern part of the city, the Defense Ministry reported.
"In Dobropolye in the Donetsk People’s Republic, units of the 51st Army, converging on the objective, have expanded the external encirclement ring in the northwestern part of the city," the ministry said in a statement.
Russia thwarts three Ukrainian attempts to break out of encirclement near Svyatogorovka
The Russian Armed Forces thwarted three Ukrainian attempts to break out of the encirclement in the city of Dobropolye toward Svyatogorovka in the Donetsk People’s Republic (DPR), the Defense Ministry reported.
"[Russian servicemen] thwarted three attempts by units of the 4th and 15th National Guard brigades and Ukraine’s 425th assault regiment to break out of the encirclement toward the town of Svyatogorovka in the Donetsk People’s Republic," the ministry said in a statement.
Russian army fights for Petropavlovka, Lozovaya, Prikolotnoye settlements, Kharkov Region
The North battlegroup is expanding its control zone near the settlements of Petropavlovka, Lozovaya, and Prikolotnoye in the Kharkov Region, the Defense Ministry said.
"Active combat operations are underway to expand the outer control zone in the areas around the settlements of Petropavlovka, Lozovaya, and Prikolotnoye in the Kharkov Region," it said in a statement.
Ukraine’s army encircled in Kharkov Region daily losses at 35 soldiers
A Ukrainian battlegroup encircled in the Kharkov Region lost more than 35 servicemen within the last 24 hours, the Russian Defense Ministry said.
"The losses of the Ukrainian armed forces units encircled [in the Kharkov Region] amounted to more than 35 servicemen over the past 24 hours," it said in a statement.

articles.title: Ukraine Has Chance to End War With Russia Before Winter, Zelenskyy Says
articles.body:
- Category
- War in Ukraine
Ukraine Has Chance to End War With Russia Before Winter, Zelenskyy Says
Ukraine has a chance to end Russia’s war before winter, but reaching that goal will depend on US political will, increased pressure on Moscow, and additional American military technology, President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said.
We bring you stories from the ground. Your support keeps our team in the field.
According to The Wall Street Journal on September 23, Zelenskyy outlined the conditions he believes could create an opportunity to reach what he described as a just peace within the next two months.
“We have a chance to stop and end this war before winter, if… There are several ‘ifs.’ Of course, the first ‘if’ is always will. The will of the United States, especially the president. It is precisely about the political will to end this war,” Zelenskyy said in the interview.
At the same time, the Ukrainian president said political will alone would not be sufficient to change Russia’s position and called for additional pressure on Vladimir Putin.
The second condition, Zelenskyy said, is access to US technology and additional weapons, particularly air defense interceptors needed to protect Ukraine during the coming winter.
“The second ‘if’ is technology. We need some technologies from the United States. We have our experience, we are always ready to share it, but we need something from the US. We need a ‘winter package’: missiles for Patriot systems. Only the US produces them now,” Zelenskyy said.
The Wall Street Journal reported that Zelenskyy raised the proposed “winter package” during his meeting with US President Donald Trump in New York on September 22, requesting additional weapons and Patriot air defense capabilities. Zelenskyy also said he expects Washington to pursue an agreement aimed at stopping attacks on energy infrastructure.
Kyiv has made additional Patriot interceptors one of its main defense priorities ahead of winter. Zelenskyy previously said Ukraine had calculated a requirement of around 300 Patriot missiles for the winter period—approximately 100 per month.
Ukraine has also been discussing licenses that would eventually allow Patriot interceptors to be produced domestically. Zelenskyy has said, however, that securing missiles for immediate use remains a higher priority because establishing new production capacity would take time.
Zelenskyy had previously said Ukraine was prepared to take reciprocal de-escalation steps if Russia stopped targeting Ukraine’s energy sector, critical infrastructure, and food exports.

articles.title: US Democrat senator urges Trump to press Xi over China-Iran ties
articles.body:
Breadcrumb
US Democratic senator urges Trump to press Xi over China-Iran ties
US Democratic Senator Jeanne Shaheen urged President Donald Trump on Wednesday to press Chinese President Xi Jinping over Beijing's support for Iran, accusing Chinese companies of providing Tehran with economic and military assistance.
The senior Democrat said Trump should use an upcoming summit with Xi to demand action against Chinese firms accused of supplying Iran with satellite imagery and components used in its missile and drone programmes, as well as helping Tehran circumvent sanctions on its oil exports.
Speaking in the Senate, Shaheen cited reports that Iran obtained high-resolution satellite imagery of a US base in Jordan from Chinese entities before carrying out a missile attack that killed three American soldiers and wounded four others.
She also pointed to China's role as the leading buyer of Iranian oil, saying around 90% of Iran's oil exports go to the country, providing Tehran with billions of dollars in revenue and a "critical economic lifeline".
Chinese and Hong Kong-based companies have also supplied components used in Iranian ballistic missiles and drones, Shaheen said.
"If we want to bring this war to an end, we need to cut off the outside support that allows Iran to keep fighting, and that starts with China," she told the Senate.
Shaheen called on Trump to "use his leverage" with Xi to stop Chinese companies from providing satellite imagery, missile and drone components and access to markets for sanctioned Iranian oil.
She also urged the Trump administration to step up enforcement of existing sanctions against Chinese entities accused of helping Iran.
"And if China doesn't stop, Congress should impose additional consequences," she said.
Shaheen linked China's relationship with Iran to its continued purchases of Russian energy, arguing that Beijing was helping finance conflicts involving both Tehran and Moscow, despite the US, alongside Israel, starting the war on Iran.
She said Trump should consider using powers contained in recently enacted legislation targeting Russia to impose penalties on Chinese buyers of Russian energy.
China was "the top funder of the war in Ukraine, as well as being one of the top funders of the war in Iran", Shaheen said.
Shaheen's call for tougher pressure on China comes despite broad public opposition to the US war with Iran, particularly among Democrats.
A Pew Research Center poll conducted in March found 59% of Americans believed the US had made the wrong decision in using military force against Iran, while 61% disapproved of Trump's handling of the conflict.
Opposition was especially strong among Democrats and Democratic-leaning independents, 88% of whom said the decision to use force was wrong and 90% of whom disapproved of Trump's handling of the war.
More recent Reuters/Ipsos polling has also found support for Trump's handling of the conflict remains weak, with only 34% approving of his strikes on Iran.

articles.title: After Trump and Zelensky meet in New York, Ukrainian president says he hopes war will end ‘before winter’
articles.body:
After Trump and Zelensky meet in New York, Ukrainian president says he hopes war will end ‘before winter’
Donald Trump and Volodymyr Zelensky met on September 22 on the sidelines of the U.N. General Assembly in New York, holding talks that lasted about 40 minutes. The two leaders discussed, among other things, prospects for negotiations with Russia, military aid to Ukraine, and a possible energy truce between Kyiv and Moscow.
Even before the meeting, Trump said from the U.N. podium that he expects the war to end soon: “We are working very closely with the leaders of Russia and Ukraine, and we will see this through to the end. It will happen, I think, sooner than people realize.”
After the talks, Zelensky also spoke about when the war might end:
I hope we will end this war, I hope that President Trump will help us end it. I think we need to do this as soon as possible — before winter, preferably before winter.
Zelensky’s hopes are shared elsewhere in Europe. “People are looking for a partial ceasefire come winter,” Finnish President Alexander Stubb said in an interview with Bloomberg.
Just two weeks earlier, speaking to Trump’s special envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner in Kyiv, Zelensky had said he expected the war to continue into winter.
In an interview with The Wall Street Journal after the meeting, Zelensky suggested that Trump would now try to reach an agreement with Moscow on an energy truce. Putin, he said, is unlikely to go along without additional pressure from Washington, such as increased sanctions. He added that Ukraine is willing to accept any format of truce and that he is ready for a three-way meeting with Putin and Trump.
The talks also covered a “winter package” of military aid. Zelensky asked Trump to give Ukraine Patriot missiles from American stockpiles, offering in exchange to later hand over to the United States part of the missiles Kyiv expects from a future delivery under an agreement with Germany. Trump did not agree, but Zelensky called the fact that he did not immediately reject the idea a “good step.”
The Kremlin said there are currently no preconditions for peace talks, though Putin is ready to meet with Trump. Presidential spokesperson Dmitry Peskov called a meeting with Zelensky without prior expert-level preparation a waste of time and reiterated that it could only take place in Moscow.
Putin said that Zelensky, if he wants, can come to Moscow. All necessary security guarantees will be provided to him. He knows very well what decisions need to be made.
Discussions about the energy truce are expected to continue on September 23, when U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio is set to meet with Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov in New York, where he arrived for the U.N. General Assembly session. The U.S. State Department announced the meeting after the Trump–Zelensky talks.
The war in photographs. Kyiv

articles.title: AI risks, Iran war dominate agenda at UN
articles.body:
AI risks, Iran war dominate agenda at UN
France convenes a UN Security Council meeting Wednesday on artificial intelligence (AI) and international security, which includes briefings by leading industry figures, including the heads of OpenAI and Anthropic. The meeting comes as world leaders jostle over how to address the risks of the new technology. On the second day of the UN General Assembly, the Iran war is also set to dominate the agenda.
To display this content from YouTube, you must enable advertisement tracking and audience measurement.
One of your browser extensions seems to be blocking the video player from loading. To watch this content, you may need to disable it on this site.
The future of Artificial intelligence and the stalled US war against Iran, with its ripple effect on the global economy, are expected to dominate the UN gathering of world leaders Wednesday.
Following weeks of worldwide headlines about risks of uncontrollable AI – and calls for a slowdown – industry leaders are set to brief a UN Security Council emergency meeting convened by France.
Sam Altman of OpenAI, Dario Amodei of Anthropic and Clement Delangue of Hugging Face will brief the 15-strong Council, the United Nation's top body.
Hugging Face, a repository of AI models, was the target of a recent cyberattack by autonomous OpenAI software, the first in a series of incidents that have raised alarm bells over the rapidly evolving technology.
Meanwhile, the annual parade of UN General Assembly speeches is set to continue, with Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian arriving late Tuesday, according to Iranian state media, to address the world body for the first time since the United States and Israel launched attacks on his country.
Read moreLive: Pezeshkian set to address UN for the first time since US, Israel launched Iran war
The strikes in late February sparked a war that engulfed the Middle East, and the Trump administration has so far yet to reach a deal with Tehran to end the conflict.
Tehran retaliated by blocking the Strait of Hormuz, a key waterway for energy transit, sparking a surge in global oil prices.
The recent Houthi takeover of Yemen's Red Sea coast has also heightened fears over global trade and shipping through the vital Bab al-Mandab Strait.
Pezeshkian's speech will come a day after Trump raised the possibility that he could "annihilate the Islamic Republic" and "drive them into hell". During his remarks, all but one member of the Iranian delegation walked out.
Ukraine, AI showdown
Trump made the comments in a fire and brimstone speech Tuesday, but he also revealed that there were talks between the two sides for the first time in months.
Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi met Trump's roving envoy Steve Witkoff and son-in-law Jared Kushner on the sidelines of the UN's signature diplomatic gathering.
Araghchi said that Tehran's demands included "the immediate lifting of the (US) naval blockade, the prompt payment of all Iranian assets that have been frozen, and an end to the war on all resistance fronts," state news agency IRIB reported.
Outside the UN on Tuesday, there was a vigil with protesters demonstrating against Tehran's use of the death penalty.
Besides conflict in the Middle East, Russia's war against Ukraine will again be raised among global diplomatic circles on Wednesday.
A Security Council meeting on Ukraine is scheduled for 11am (15:00 GMT), while President Volodymyr Zelensky is due to address the UN General Assembly as well.
Zelensky, after meeting with Trump on Tuesday, said that Washington and Kyiv want the war with Russia to end "before winter".
He added that he is ready to halt strikes on Russian energy sites if Moscow agreed to do the same.
In his speech Tuesday, Trump rejected international regulation of AI, calling such proposals a "globalist scheme".
"The very same people who said we'll all be dead in 12 years because of global warming ... are now saying that AI is going to kill us all," Trump said.
But just hours after Trump spoke, Macron took to the rostrum and defiantly called for the creation of an open-source AI model not dependent on the United States or China.
"I don't want anyone to become the vassal of one of the great powers," he said. "Rather, we must come together to build an open-source frontier model, a cutting-edge model."
(FRANCE 24 with AFP)

articles.title: Nuclear arms unlikely to be deployed in Lithuania soon despite parliament consent — expert
articles.body:
MOSCOW, September 23. /TASS/. Nuclear weapons will not appear on Lithuanian territory in the near future, despite the decision by the Seimas (parliament) to lift the ban on their deployment, Ruslan Pankratov, a member of the Officers of Russia expert council, deputy chairman of the Union of Political Emigrants of Europe, and a former deputy of the Riga City Council has said.
On September 22, the Lithuanian Seimas approved lifting the ban on the deployment of nuclear weapons within the country. Following a discussion of the issue, the parliament referred a constitutional amendment to the relevant committees for review.
"There is a vast, if not enormous, gap between repealing Article 137 and the actual arrival of nuclear weapons on Lithuanian soil. Decisions to deploy nuclear warheads would require specific consent from the US and NATO, military infrastructure, specialized security and storage procedures, and would entail significant political costs," Pankratov said.
In his opinion, such decisions amount to an "ostentatious demonstration of Lithuania's readiness for the closest possible military-political integration with NATO."
Pankratov also emphasized that the practical value of deploying nuclear warheads in Lithuania for NATO is quite limited.
"The alliance is unlikely to rush the deployment of nuclear weapons right on the Russian and Belarusian borders, as this would sharply increase the risk of actual - rather than merely rhetorical - escalation for its domestic electorate," he explained.

articles.title: ‘A triumph of money, filth, and hypocrisy’: EU decision to lift sanctions on Russian billionaires Fridman and Usmanov draws backlash
articles.body:
‘A triumph of money, filth, and hypocrisy’: EU decision to lift sanctions on Russian billionaires Fridman and Usmanov draws backlash
The European Union maintains a large sanctions list drawn up in response to Russia’s aggression against Ukraine. It includes more than 3,000 people and companies. EU countries used to review the list every six months. On September 22, they agreed to extend it for a full three years, but with an important caveat: two billionaires with close ties to Russia, Mikhail Fridman and Alisher Usmanov, were removed from the list. Both men had long sought to have the sanctions lifted, both through European courts and other means. The final decision on their cases was political rather than judicial: Luxembourg intervened on behalf of Fridman, who has filed a lawsuit against the country for a huge sum, while France intervened for Usmanov and, in exchange, received a pardon for one of its citizens who had been convicted in Azerbaijan.
The lifting of European restrictions on Fridman and Usmanov has outraged figures in the Russian opposition in exile, Ukrainian officials, and some European politicians. Meduza has collected their reactions, presented here with minor cuts.
Russian opposition
Vladimir Kara-Murza
opposition politician
Shame on you [in the European Union].
Yulia Navalnaya
leader of the Navalny-founded Anti-Corruption Foundation
It turns out that for Europe, it doesn’t matter whether you support the war or not, or whether you’re friends with Putin or opposed to him. In the end, it seems, what matters far more is how much money is in your bank accounts.
If you’re rich, have a couple of yachts and the right connections, apparently your sanctions can be lifted without much trouble. But if you fled Russia with little more than a few belongings because of political persecution or the draft, because you don’t support the war, it’s a different story: you might be denied a visa, refused a bank account, faced with a mountain of obstacles, and effectively pushed back into the arms of Putin’s system. And accused of supporting the war on top of it.
Thanks to the European Commission for yet another reminder that in big politics, money still speaks louder than principles, and the fates of ordinary people often end up somewhere near the bottom of the list of priorities.
Leonid Volkov
head of political projects at the Anti-Corruption Foundation
On Fridman, this is simply a mistake. He hasn’t done anything, hasn’t changed anything, hasn’t even spoken up. Lifting his sanctions “just because” is foolish. Four years ago I proposed, and I still believe, that clear and transparent mechanisms should have been created for exiting sanctions for entrepreneurs like Fridman, in exchange for concrete steps to weaken Putin’s regime: everything from condemning the war to providing substantial help to Ukraine. That was entirely achievable, but it was never done.
On Usmanov, this isn’t just a mistake, it’s a moral catastrophe, and a double one at that. First, Usmanov is no “rank-and-file oligarch.” He is one of the key people in the system. And it’s not just that his personal kept man is former president and current drunken bully Medvedev, but also which assets Usmanov bought up on behalf of and at the direction of the Kremlin for censorship and lawlessness: from MegaFon to Kommersant. Remember: “I don’t use the internet, I develop it”? Well, Usmanov is one of the people who developed it into its current state.
Second, Usmanov achieved the lifting of sanctions through hostage-taking. Azerbaijani dictator Aliyev helped out as a friend, detained French citizens, and France came running to sort things out. Great! The path out of sanctions has been shown: expect new hostages!
In 2022, Leonid Volkov signed a letter to the European Commission asking that sanctions against Mikhail Fridman and other senior Alfa Group executives be lifted. The letter proposed that the EU adopt “a clear and simple set of criteria” for removing people from the sanctions list. “These criteria could be tied to a public condemnation of the war, compensation for damages, and severing ties with Putin and his regime,” the letter said.
The letter became public in 2023. Volkov called it his “major political mistake” and stepped down as head of the international Anti-Corruption Foundation, ACF International, though he remained one of its key figures.
Meduza wrote in detail about this story here.
Maria Pevchikh
former head of the investigations department at the Anti-Corruption Foundation
What a colossal, planetary-scale disgrace this lifting of sanctions on Fridman and Usmanov is. As I said a couple of years ago, when I proposed trading yachts for political prisoners (which for some reason caused quite a scandal), if that isn’t done, the sanctions will simply be lifted for nothing. There will be no yachts and no political prisoners released. That is exactly what is happening now.
A triumph of money, filth, and hypocrisy. Some people, to get a measly work visa in Europe, have to bend over backwards proving they’re sufficiently anti-war, that none of their relatives, down to a seventh cousin, work for Putin’s regime, and produce stacks of convictions handed down in absentia in Russia. But these two assholes, pardon my language, haven’t said a single word against the war, and yet, please, come on in, cruise around on your yacht, live in your villas, no problem at all.
Vyacheslav Gimadi
head of the legal department at the Anti-Corruption Foundation
Putin’s oligarchs Usmanov (against whom I won at the European Court of Human Rights over Navalny’s investigation into Medvedev’s corruption) and the no less notorious Fridman are being removed from EU sanctions. How could this happen? These decisions are made unanimously, meaning any of the 27 countries can block them regardless of the “interests of the majority.” That’s what the Hungarians, Austrians, and Slovaks did, and now apparently France too, from what I’ve read. This vulnerability and pliability, I believe, diminish the institution itself, since it encourages terrorists to pressure individual countries, or maybe even offer them [financial] incentives, though I have no proof of that, and to blackmail them. Other people on the list will surely want to follow the same successful path.
Ivan Zhdanov
former director of the Anti-Corruption Foundation
If the European Union adopts this decision (or has already adopted it), it will collapse the entire system of personal sanctions. Today I sent an urgent letter through whatever channels I had, describing Usmanov’s personal role in the persecution of Navalny and of me (my first criminal case was over Usmanov) and his funding of the warmonger Medvedev. A terrible injustice and an abandonment of its own values [on the part of the European Union].
Alexey Navalny had long been in conflict with Alisher Usmanov. Their dispute began in 2017, when the Anti-Corruption Foundation released an investigation titled On vam ne Dimon “He Is Not Dimon to You,” about Dmitry Medvedev’s alleged corruption. The film said that Usmanov had given a charitable foundation linked to Medvedev a mansion in the Rublyovka area. Navalny called this a bribe, and Usmanov sued him and won. The court ordered the film removed from all platforms, but Navalny and his associates never complied.
In 2022, after Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine, the Anti-Corruption Foundation published a “list of corrupt officials and warmongers” naming 6,000 people. The foundation proposed adding them to Western sanctions lists for strengthening Putin’s regime and supporting Russia’s invasion of Ukraine. Usmanov, like Fridman, is on this list.
That history may explain why current and former Anti-Corruption Foundation representatives have been so vocal in criticizing the decision to lift sanctions on Fridman and Usmanov.
Ukrainian authorities
Volodymyr Zelensky
president of Ukraine
At a time when Russia is carrying out brutal attacks on our people – and even now, during the UN General Assembly, air raid alerts are ongoing in many regions because of drones and ballistic missiles – signals about lifting sanctions on individual Russian oligarchs are self-defeating and counterproductive. Wars end through resolve and strength, not concessions to the aggressor’s entourage. I’m grateful to [European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen] for her readiness to work on adding more Russian names to the EU sanctions lists. These are the kinds of steps that bring a just peace and guaranteed security closer.
Andrii Sybiha
foreign minister of Ukraine
The decision to remove Usmanov and Fridman from the sanctions list is shameful and entirely unjustified. Moscow is celebrating, having gotten exactly what it wanted: a sense of impunity, the humiliation of the European Union, and a split among Europeans. I call on all EU member states to declare now that they will impose their own national sanctions against these two individuals.
Vladyslav Vlasiuk
Ukrainian presidential commissioner for sanctions policy
We consider the EU’s decision not to extend sanctions against Alisher Usmanov and Mikhail Fridman very strange. […] Lifting restrictions on individual Russian businessmen should not become a new practice. That is why we will keep proposing new sanctions measures, in particular regarding Russian oligarchs connected to Russia’s military-industrial complex.
European politicians
Pina Picierno
vice president of the European Parliament
The decision to delist Usmanov and Fridman is disgraceful, cowardly and completely unacceptable. But let’s be crystal clear about where political responsibility lies: with the Member States in the Council, not the Commission.
Under the EU treaties (such rules that must change!), the High Representative proposes sanctions, working with the Commission on their economic aspects. But restrictive measures can only be adopted unanimously by the Council.
This unanimity rule makes the EU fragile and weak. We need a politically strong, sovereign Europe: one that is more than the sum of its Member States.
Andris Kulbergs
head of Latvia’s government
Latvia agreed to a compromise but is not changing its principled stance.
We opposed the removal of Alisher Usmanov and Mikhail Fridman from the European Union’s sanctions list until the very end. […] However, the government had to make a responsible decision. The choice was between changing the status of two individuals and risking the loss of the entire sanctions regime. That is why Latvia’s representative will abstain in the vote. […]
Latvia is not backing down. The Foreign Ministry has been instructed to prepare the legal grounds for imposing national sanctions against Usmanov and Fridman.
Mindaugas Sinkevičius
prime minister of Lithuania
Oligarchs are part of Russia’s war machine. The regime’s “wallets” must not be allowed to feel at ease in Europe while Ukrainians are being killed. I have instructed the relevant authorities to initiate the process for imposing national restrictive measures on Alisher Usmanov and Mikhail Fridman.
Margus Tsahkna
foreign minister of Estonia
The EU has just extended sanctions against nearly 3,000 individuals and entities linked to Russia’s aggression for another three years. This is a significant achievement, as it reduces the risk of future sanctions renewals becoming hostage to political bargaining.
However, to secure this agreement, sanctions against two prominent Russian businessmen, Alisher Usmanov and Mikhail Fridman, both known supporters of Russia’s aggression against Ukraine, were lifted.
Estonia did not support this decision and abstained from the vote. We will now impose national sanctions on both individuals. Russia has not changed course. Neither should we.
Maciej Wąsik
member of the European Parliament from Poland
A compromising of the EU. Russian billionaires Usmanov and Fridman have been removed from the sanctions list. Only Latvia protested. Where was the Polish government? Where was the Polish protest?
At Meduza, we are committed to transparency about our use of artificial intelligence in the newsroom. articles.title: Baltic states try secret dip into EU defense purse – media
articles.body:
Baltic states try secret dip into EU defense purse – media
The Baltic states have secretly asked the European Commission for hundreds of millions of euros to boost their defense against drones, citing an alleged Russian threat, Lithuania’s Defence Minister Robertas Kaunas told to Reuters on Wednesday.
Moscow has repeatedly rejected claims that it has aggressive designs against Europe, saying that they are only made by Western politicians to scare the population at home and justify growing military spending. It maintains that a conflict is only possible if NATO members attack Russia.
Finnish newspaper Iltalehti said on Tuesday, citing foreign policy and security sources, that the defense ministers of Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania had sent a letter to EU chief Ursula von der Leyen the previous day, asking Brussels to urgently provide them with €500 million (around $570 million). There has been no public announcement about the request being made, it added.
The minister claimed that the funds are needed due to the possibility of Russia trying to test NATO’s resolve by carrying out drone strikes against the bloc’s eastern flank, the report read.
Tallinn, Riga and Vilnius expect a positive response from von der Leyen in a matter of weeks, with the money arriving by the end of the year, according to the sources.
Last week, Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk said that Russia could fire drones or missiles into NATO countries backing Ukraine in “the next few months.” Despite Tusk providing no proof to his claim, French President Emmanuel Macron described it as “sound and well-documented.”
On Tuesday, Lithuanian Prime Minister Mindaugas Sinkevicius told the BBC that his country feels “constantly threatened” by Russia because of drones entering its airspace.
Since spring, there have been a number of incidents of Ukrainian UAVs crossing into Lithuania, Latvia and Estonia or crashing in their territory as Kiev has intensified its long-range attacks on energy infrastructure in Leningrad Region in northwestern Russia.
The Baltic states claimed that the incursions happened because of the UAVs being diverted off course by Russian electronic warfare equipment. Moscow has warned Tallinn, Riga and Vilnius that it could act in accordance with its right to self-defense if it turns out that the three countries are knowingly providing their airspace to the Ukrainian military.
Latvian President Edgars Rinkevics claimed in an interview with the Kiev Independent the same day that his country is facing an “alarming” period due to possible Russian interference in the wake of an election on October 3.
On Wednesday, high-ranking Estonian Foreign Ministry official Jonatan Vseviov said that warnings of an alleged Russian attack on the Baltic states were “blown out of proportion.” According to Vseviov, Moscow “ultimately seeks… to change the entire European security architecture,” but it’s currently fully focused on the Ukraine conflict.
Russian President Vladimir Putin said last week that “some European leaders are openly declaring that they are preparing for war with Russia” in an attempt to “cover up mistakes in their economic and social policies.”
“Instead of stopping and listening to their citizens, who have made it clear during the elections that they don’t want any war with Russia, these leaders continue to escalate the situation,” Putin stressed.

articles.title: Russia’s sanctioned propaganda network Rybar freely roamed Schengen zone to shoot manipulative content
articles.body:
Russia's propaganda center Rybar ran a covert filming operation across multiple European countries, Ukraine's Center for Countering Disinformation (CCD) reported, citing a Czech investigation by Seznam Zprávy. The founder of the project, Mykhailo Zvinchuk, has been under sanctions by the European Union and the UK.
The EU's sanctions justification states that Rybar is a member of a working group established by Vladimir Putin in December 2022 to coordinate Russia's mobilization efforts in connection with the war against Ukraine.
Moscow has recently escalated covert influence operations and disinformation across Europe, yet years of sanctions have not stopped its operatives from working inside the EU. The Rybar case shows how thin the enforcement of those measures remains.
Rybar crew posed as documentarians in Prague
Russians moved freely within the Schengen Area, holding residence permits for EU countries, particularly Germany. They traveled to Prague posing as documentary filmmakers and attempted to record interviews with local experts and politicians. The stated pretext was a documentary series on Europe's sociopolitical situation.
When Seznam Zprávy journalists confronted the film crew at the meeting location, the propagandists fled. The investigation identified Boris Dvorkin as the Moscow-based producer of the operation. One of his projects received funding from the History of the Fatherland Foundation, established by Putin's decree and headed by Sergei Naryshkin, chief of Russia's Foreign Intelligence Service (SVR).
Operations planned across multiple countries
Similar filming operations were allegedly planned or already carried out in Czechia, Slovakia, Austria, Hungary, Serbia, France, and other countries, the CCD said.
The UK sanctioned Rybar and Zvinchuk in December 2025, citing the network's interference in elections in Moldova and Armenia. It added ten more Rybar staff members in July 2026 for their role in destabilizing Ukraine. In 2024, the US State Department offered a $10 million reward for information on Zvinchuk and eight others tied to the project.
